terms.comment: A description of ours: a suitcase fitted with wheels. No reference work has a word for it. The attested adjective for a thing on wheels is subrotātus (Vitr. 10.13.4, in M-O s.v. skate: roller-skate, roller-blade, in-line skate; Traupman 346, of a mobile home).

phrases.latin: Vidulus autem, quia rotīs īnstrūctus est, nōn portātur sed trahitur
phrases.english: The suitcase, though, having wheels, isn’t carried but pulled

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. skate: roller-skate, roller-blade, in-line skate.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 346.
